title: Florida Atlantic University Receives NIST Grant to Build South Florida Quantum Cybersecurity Workforce Ecosystem - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Florida Atlantic University (FAU), in collaboration with dual-platform quantum hardware provider D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS), has received a $200,000 cooperative agreement award from the U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Awarded through NIST’s Regional Alliances and Multistakeholder Partnerships to Stimulate (RAMPS) Cybersecurity Education and Workforce Development program, the grant funds the establishment of a regional quantum cybersecurity workforce consortium across South Florida.

The initiative, titled “Building the Quantum Cybersecurity Workforce in the Palm Beach and Treasure Coast Region,” integrates quantum computing, cybersecurity, and critical energy infrastructure protection. Led by FAU’s College of Engineering and Computer Science and the Florida Power & Light (FPL) Center for Intelligent Energy Technologies (InETech), the program develops hands-on workshops, case studies, and training modules aligned with the NICE Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity. The curriculum leverages FAU’s upcoming on-premises deployment of a dedicated 4,400+ qubit D-Wave Advantage2™ annealing quantum system on its Boca Raton campus.

The consortium connects academia, private sector critical infrastructure partners via the InfraGard South Florida Members Alliance, and K-12 school districts. By pairing real-world power grid simulation environments with quantum annealing access, the partnership establishes a workforce pipeline trained to secure critical infrastructure against emerging post-quantum cryptographic threats.
